title: Build a Split Plan
bottom_line: Run /plan-tools:plan-split-implment in a repo with a split plan, and Claude builds each remaining session in turn, committing each one on a plan branch.

sections.heading: Start it in a repo that already has a split plan

blocks.caption: Without --branch, the work goes on a branch named plan/<feature-name>.

cards.title: A split plan exists
cards.text: `.planning/progress.md` and `.planning/sessions/`, as written by /plan-tools:split-plan. If they are missing, Claude checks the project root, then asks you.

cards.title: Blockers only you can clear
cards.text: Steps that need your own credentials, accounts or access. Claude lists them before it starts any session.

terms.definition: One chunk of the plan, with its own file in `.planning/sessions/`. Only sessions not yet complete are run.
A separate helper Claude starts for one job. Here, one subagent builds one session.
A separate line of work in git, so changes stay off the main code until they are merged.
A saved snapshot of the code changes, with a message.

blocks.title: Where it fits
blocks.caption: The README's example for an existing repo with a plan.

sections.heading: Work goes on a plan branch, never straight onto main

before.label: You are on main
before.text: On `main` or `master`, Claude first creates an implementation branch, such as `plan/<feature-name>`, and works there.

after.label: With --branch
after.text: Claude uses the name you give instead of `plan/<feature-name>`.

blocks.text: Every session ends with a commit, and those commits belong on a branch, not on main.

sections.heading: Claude lists anything that needs your own access, then waits

blocks.title: The blocker check

nodes.label: Only a numbered checklist, one line each

blocks.caption: With no blockers it says so in one line and starts without waiting for a go-ahead.

blocks.title: Examples of blockers
items: Signing up for or logging into a third-party service.
Creating an API key or OAuth app.
Granting a permission or dashboard access.
Any manual action in a UI.

sections.heading: Sessions run one at a time, each in its own helper

steps.title: Reads the plan conventions
steps.text: It reads `.planning/CLAUDE.md`, then its own session file.

steps.title: Does the session's tasks
steps.text: It carries out the tasks exactly as written.

steps.title: Updates the project CLAUDE.md
steps.text: It records what changed this session in the project's root CLAUDE.md, creating the file if it does not exist yet.

steps.title: Commits
steps.text: It commits the work, including the CLAUDE.md update.

steps.title: Marks progress
steps.text: It marks its session complete in `.planning/progress.md` and the next one active.

steps.title: Exits
steps.text: The next session starts only after this one finishes and `progress.md` confirms it.

blocks.text: Sessions never run in parallel, because each depends on the one before. Each helper reads `.planning/CLAUDE.md` for the plan's conventions. Claude itself never writes code here; it only hands out sessions and watches them.

sections.heading: Questions come to you; a broken session stops the run

cards.title: A helper has a question
cards.text: A session can hit a decision its plan does not answer.

points.text: Claude asks you in plain English and passes your answer back so the helper continues.

cards.title: A session breaks
cards.text: A session fails or ends in a broken state.

points.text: Claude stops and reports to you. It does not skip ahead to the next session.

sections.heading: At the end, CLAUDE.md is tidied and the plan is archived

steps.title: Improve CLAUDE.md
steps.text: Runs `/claude-md-management:claude-md-improver` on the root CLAUDE.md if the `claude-md-management` plugin is installed. Otherwise it skips this and says so.

steps.title: Compress CLAUDE.md
steps.text: Runs `/caveman:caveman-compress claude.md` if the `caveman` plugin is installed. Otherwise it skips this and says so.

steps.title: Sync user flows
steps.text: If `user-flows.md` exists at the project root, runs `/user-flows:update-user-flows` to match everything built, then commits. Skipped when the file does not exist.

steps.title: Archive the plan
steps.text: Moves the plan's `.md` files and `sessions/` into a feature-named folder inside the plan location, so it is clean for the next plan. The move is not committed, because the plan location is almost always ignored by git.

reference.title: Default branch name
items: Plan work happens on a branch named `plan/<feature-name>`. This default is shared by `plan-split-implment` and `plan-implement-complete`, and you change it with `--branch <name>`.

reference.title: About the plan-tools plugin
items: Plugin purpose: plan-driven workflow tools that bootstrap a new web or mobile app end to end, split implementation plans into context-sized resumable sessions, and drive them to PRs.
Installing plan-tools also installs the plugins it depends on: `ntfy`, `fastapi-template` and `htmx-vs-alpine`.

No environment variables are needed. The one setting, `designer_ui_review` (default `false`), is changed with `/plugin configure plan-tools@wovemind`. It runs the ui-change-guard designer review (/ui-change-guard:review-ui-change) before finalize-pr raises a PR.

next_action.text: Run /plan-tools:plan-split-implment in the repo that holds your .planning folder.
next_action.detail: Add --branch <name> if you want a branch name other than plan/<feature-name>.
